content.text: The text reviews digestive disorders, emphasizing individualized diet, regular meals, thorough chewing, hygiene, fresh air, exercise, rest, and mental wellbeing. It discusses artificially digested foods, pepsin, pancreatic preparations, bitters, acids, bismuth, iron, and other historical remedies. Gastralgia is described as episodic neuralgic epigastric pain, often linked to anaemia, hysteria, malaria, visceral disease, or emotional stress. Acute and chronic gastritis involve inflammation, nausea, vomiting, tenderness, impaired appetite, and nutritional decline; treatment stresses gastric rest and bland, restricted diets. Gastric ulcer typically causes meal-related localized pain, vomiting, bleeding, anaemia, perforation, and possible scarring or obstruction; treatment centers on rest, milk or other gentle nourishment, and cautious symptom control. Gastric cancer causes progressive dyspepsia, vomiting, pain, weight loss, cachexia, bleeding, and sometimes a palpable tumor. Sandra travelled to the bathroom.
